conclusion: No blocking implementation finding remains in the reviewed management/inspection/retention/CLI scope. New cleanup-failure test validates the fixed catch-scope and real adapter cleanup; complete prepared inventories and portable metadata checks pass.

unchangedGodotGeneratorAndRuntimeSources.scope: Godot adapter cleanup intentionally changed; the existing generator/runtime sources listed here remain byte identical.

nativeManifest.scope: Byte verification here; tool/native runtime execution belongs to separate owner logs, not this review.

independentFinal.scope: CLI uses bounded executable contract fixtures; retention uses actual host writes with injected phases. No actual Godot/Bevy engine acceptance claimed by these 16 tests.

prepared.scope: Actual prepared desktop/mobile copies: complete byte inventories, portable metadata validation, and copied desktop CLI inspection of a disposable output. No tool/build process, installation, Android device, GUI or foreign-platform acceptance here.
prepared.vmScope: Standard Node VM without Node/DOM/network globals proves portability of copied pure metadata code; it is not a security sandbox for hostile code.

verifiedBoundaries: Portable manifests describe source/backend/adapter/tool identity, generated files/resource copies, exact metadata evidence and lifecycle; they do not grant filesystem, execution, plugin installation or cleanup authority.

Inspect uses frozen source and registered implementation fingerprints without consulting the author workspace or identifying/starting a tool. Missing legacy manifest derives a read-only description without adoption or repair.

Unknown directories are reported as single extra entries and never traversed. Known artifacts/metadata are checked before and after asynchronous generator work. Added manual/session paths make completeness false rather than becoming owned files.

Service selects only its own successful-build UUID for inspection. Inspection DTOs and in-flight completions remain bound to the selected owned entry, root identity and frozen build/snapshot/manifest pins.

Management inventory validation and runtime authorization stay separate: runtime preserves the existing frozen-byte, backend, adapter and tool checks. complete=false does not itself revoke runtime admission.

Cleanup authority is a private, current-service write receipt with physical root/inode and exact byte/tree inventory. Extra/manual/session paths, edits, symlinks, hardlinks and replaced roots preserve outputs.

Retirement quarantines the exact owned directory then repeats the complete content/ownership check before deletion. Deterministic mutations at rename and outside links were tested; new builds remain successful when old outputs are preserved.

Godot cleanup only removes .godot/.host cache classes and exact staged script .uid/resource .import paths. Failure retains partial project inputs and unrelated files, attempts known cleanup once, writes failed record, and publishes no successful manifest.

Copied desktop CLI inspects a disposable generated output while author files are offline; copied mobile pure code validates the four actual backend manifests without importing or executing Node backend host modules.

resolvedFindings.resolution: CLI derives tool configuration from the frozen backend for run and suite; explicit tool/backends and Godot alias admission remain enforced.
Root added private receipts, dirty/session/link preservation, same-parent quarantine and second complete check. No scan/adopt of previous sessions.
resolvedFindings.proof: 4 original boundary tests plus owner retention logs

resolvedFindings.resolution: Root moved adapter/generated to outer build scope so catch cleanup is reachable. The new fifth boundary test observes one cleanup call after an injected thrown phase and checks cache/known sidecars removed, partial/unrelated files retained.

preservedInitialEvidence.classification: New CLI fixture assumed upstream author reader accepted a colon/newline path; upstream world reader rejected it. Fixture narrowed to pure audit-path semantics, no product path-permission expansion.
Revised legacy executable fixture exceeded existing frozen-planner permission; corrected to pure portable audit validation.
New failure cleanup fixture used positional executePhase arguments; actual host API passes one object. Test-only repair.
New cleanup spy expected generator-only paths but actual trusted staged set also includes resource copies. Test-only repair.
Root focused initial run included the same new cleanup fixture expectation failure; log remains unchanged.
Proof wrongly expected standard VM built-in WebAssembly to be absent. Corrected assertion covers Node/DOM/network globals; no WASM or runtime invocation occurs in pure metadata proof.
Initial owner native build lacked prepared resources; repair has a distinct log.

Actual Godot outputs initially reported known UID/import extras; cleanup was added. Initial real smoke also used an unregistered Bevy ID, corrected only in the new fixture. Final four real manifest receipts report complete inventories.

limitations: Only current service-session history/ownership is managed; previous caches are not adopted and there is no persistent cross-service history or editable generated author project.

Retirement is protected against the bounded tested filesystem changes and ordinary path writers; it is not a transaction lock against arbitrary continuous same-user concurrent writes after the final check.
Prepared VM is a portability test, not a hostile-code security sandbox. No mobile Node backend execution, Android device, installed Tauri application or foreign-platform acceptance.

The added fifth boundary case was introduced after the full-check initial file enumeration may have completed. Its actual acceptance is the separate final 16-case log and the root focused rerun; do not inflate the initial full-check count.
